text:
anika: Quick update from today's activation-blend run (mixing SmoothQuant + activation-aware scaling) on the 70B longspan reference. Context=128k, compared FP16 baseline, FP8 (AWQ), GPTQ INT8, and the new activation-blend profile. Posting a short summary with numbers and a recommended rollout.

josh: Nice — which eval sets did you use?

anika: Eval sets = stories-lm (perplexity), long-code (pass@1), convqa (EM/F1), and a small downstream ranking test. 1200 examples total, stratified by length.

marcel: TL;DR numbers?

anika: TL;DR: FP16 baseline is still best for absolute quality, but activation-blend narrows the gap with much of the latency/cost upside.
- Perplexity (stories-lm):
  - FP16 baseline: 2.31
  - FP8 (AWQ weights, act unscaled): 2.35 (+0.04)
  - GPTQ INT8: 2.40 (+0.09)
  - activation-blend (AWQ weights + act-aware per-layer scale): 2.33 (+0.02)
- Long-code pass@1:
  - FP16: 78.2%
  - FP8: 76.1% (-2.1)
  - GPTQ INT8: 73.9% (-4.3)
  - activation-blend: 77.5% (-0.7)
- convQA (EM): FP16 68.4 / activation-blend 67.9 (-0.5)

josh: Nice gap closing on code. What about latency / p99?

anika: Measured on the same dedicated GPU pool (A100-p4-equivalent) with token-at-a-time generation and KV cache warm. Per-token latency median/p95/p99 (ms):
- FP16: 12 / 89 / 110
- FP8: 10 / 78 / 95
- GPTQ INT8: 9 / 72 / 88
- activation-blend: 10 / 75 / 92
Throughput (tokens/sec, batch=4): FP16 210, FP8 260, GPTQ 285, activation-blend 270.

priya: Memory/kv cache footprint? Any change to eviction behavior at 128k?

anika: KV memory peak (GB) for a single 70B instance with 128k context: FP16 ~220GB, FP8 ~145GB, GPTQ ~130GB, activation-blend ~150GB. We saw similar eviction profiles between FP8 and activation-blend; GPTQ had slightly better cache packing but worse quality on code.

marcel: Were any prompts showing large regressions?

anika: One cluster of long code completions (~12% of the code eval) had a larger drop for GPTQ (-9 pass@1) and FP8 (-6) while activation-blend only dropped -1.5. Those prompts are heavy on repeated identifiers and deep nesting — probably activation-scale sensitivity there.

elena: For rollout, recommend canary on Dedicated first, not hosted API. If metrics hold, expand. Also add a quick regression alert that triggers if pass@1 drops >1.5 or perplexity delta >0.03 over baseline for any route.

anika: Agreed. Proposed rollout: canary 5% (dedicated), monitor story-perplexity, code pass@1, and p99 latency. 24h hold. Auto-fallback to FP16 or FP8 (depending on capacity) if thresholds exceeded.

priya: Can you paste the exact run command and the eval bucket?

anika: Sure:
```
./run_bakeoff --model 70B-longspan --ctx 128k --quant activation-blend --eval sets=stories-lm,long-code,convqa --bs 1 --seed 42 --out /tmp/actblend-run-2187
```
Eval bucket: gs://redwood-evals/eng-ml/actblend/2026-03-18/

deploy-bot: Canary deploy request queued: service=dedicated-70b, image=70b-actblend:v1, traffic=5%, expires_in=24h. Monitor: /dash/models/70b/actblend/rollout.

marcel: Any notes on config knobs (batching / kernel choices) we should pin?

anika: Yes — important bits:
- kernel: prefer fp8-friendly GEMM kernels for prefix layers, fallback int8 kernels for last few layers where act-scale saturates.
- batcher: cap at 4 for tail-latency stability at 128k.
- kv eviction policy: LRU with 1% headroom buffer for actblend runs.
- quant calib: use layer-wise second-moment statistics collected from long-span corpus (not short prompts).

josh: Who's owning the canary and alert config?

elena: I'll own the canary setup and alerts. Priya will own the regression rules. Anika will push the run notebook and config.

anika: I'll upload the notebook + full table (per-prompt deltas) to the eval bucket and add a short README with reproduction steps.

priya: One more ask — can we add automated prompt-level diffs for the code cluster that regressed so SRE/SEs can triage?

anika: Yep, adding a small script that dumps token-level diffs and top-10 n-gram mismatches.

elena: Sounds good. If canary looks stable we can promote to 20% and then 50% over a week. Keep the fallback in place.

anika: Thanks all — I'll follow up with the notebook link in this thread once uploaded. :rocket:
